title: Group Policy: which settings reach Windows users and computers in Active Directory, and who sets them
summary: Hold: the page makes the Central Store mandatory even though Microsoft documents local template storage as an alternative. The domain editor refresh path omits Policies, and the timing statements omit distinctions between Active Directory and SYSVOL replication and exceptions to Office restart requirements.

claims.claim: In Group Policy Management Console, Site, domain or OU > Link an Existing GPO links an existing GPO.
claims.quote: Right-click a site, domain, or OU item, and then select Link an Existing GPO.

claims.claim: New-GPO -Name <GPO name> | New-GPLink -Target <distinguished name of site, domain or OU> -LinkEnabled Yes creates and links a GPO.
claims.quote: New-GPO -Name "MyGPO" | New-GPLink -Target "ou=MyOU,dc=contoso,dc=com" -LinkEnabled Yes

claims.claim: Group Policy Management Editor > Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge reaches the Edge policies.
claims.quote: To configure a mandatory policy, open the Group Policy Editor and go to (Computer Configuration or User Configuration) > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.
claims.fix: The path stops at the policy list. Extend it to 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > policy', with a lower-case placeholder for the policy selected, as described by https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-policy/group-policy-management-console.

claims.claim: Set-GPRegistryValue -Name <GPO name> -Key <registry key> -ValueName <value name> -Value <value> -Type <type> configures registry-based policy in a GPO.
claims.quote: One or more registry values by passing the Key, ValueName, Value, and Type parameters.

claims.claim: Group Policy Management Console > Group Policy Objects > GPO > Scope > Security Filtering reaches security filtering.
claims.quote: In GPMC, on the Scope tab for the GPO, you add contoso_user_group to the Security Filtering list.

claims.claim: Set-GPPermission -Name <GPO name> -PermissionLevel GpoApply -TargetName <group name> -TargetType Group grants a group GPO application permissions.
claims.quote:
Set-GPPermission
    [-Name] <String>
    -PermissionLevel <GPPermissionType>
    -TargetName <String>
    -TargetType <PermissionTrusteeType>

claims.claim: In Group Policy Management Editor, Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Group Policy > Set Group Policy refresh interval for computers is the domain GPO route.
claims.quote: Go to Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > System > Group Policy > Set Group Policy refresh interval for computers'. The cited CSP maps the setting to System > Group Policy; the domain editor hierarchy in https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/evaluate-mdav-using-gp includes Policies between Computer Configuration and Administrative Templates.

claims.claim: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ADMX_GroupPolicy/GroupPolicyRefreshRate configures computer background Group Policy refresh through MDM.
claims.quote: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ADMX_GroupPolicy/GroupPolicyRefreshRate

claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Import ADMX tab > Import:

claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/groupPolicyUploadedDefinitionFiles
content | Binary | The contents of the uploaded ADMX file.
claims.fix: Keep the call and add to the row note: 'The request body sets content to the ADMX file contents and groupPolicyUploadedLanguageFiles to its associated ADML files.' Both properties are documented at the existing Graph reference URL.

claims.claim: By default only domain administrators and enterprise administrators can link GPOs to domains and OUs.
claims.quote: By default, only domain administrators and enterprise administrators have this privilege for domains and OUs.

claims.claim: Set-GPRegistryValue configures the registry value that the client receives when the GPO applies.
claims.quote: The policy setting configures keys or values in the registry on the client computer when the GPO is applied.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Out-of-date Central Store
claims.claim: The template must be in the Central Store before a new setting can appear in the editor.
claims.quote: Alternatively, add these rules and settings to the Policy Definition template folder on individual computers and then configure the specific policies you want to set.
claims.fix: Replace the row note's last sentence with 'Install the templates in the Central Store, or in the Policy Definition template folder on individual computers.' Narrow the corresponding Why it matters and Risks and limits sentences to 'When using a Central Store, copy updated templates into it before configuring newly added policies.' Microsoft documents the alternative at https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge.

claims.claim: Group Policy is a Windows feature for centralized configuration of operating systems, applications and user settings.
claims.quote: Group Policy is a feature of Windows that provides centralized management and configuration of operating systems, applications, and user settings.

claims.claim: Administrators store domain Group Policy settings in a Group Policy Object.
claims.quote: When you use Group Policy with Active Directory (AD), you store Group Policy settings in a Group Policy Object (GPO).

claims.claim: The Group Policy container component is stored in the domain partition of Active Directory.
claims.quote: The Group Policy container is stored in the domain partition of Active Directory

claims.claim: The Group Policy template component is stored in SYSVOL on each domain controller.
claims.quote: the Group Policy template is located in the SYSVOL folder on each domain controller (DC).

claims.claim: GPO settings are categorized as computer settings and user settings.
claims.quote: Policy settings are categorized into those that apply to a computer and those that apply to a user.

claims.claim: Client-side extensions apply GPO settings, including registry updates.
claims.quote: A Client-side extension (CSE) applies the specific settings dictated by the GPOs, managing tasks like registry updates and security configurations.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Links and precedence; mechanism table
claims.claim: Linking GPOs to Active Directory sites, domains and OUs determines which users and computers are in scope.
claims.quote: By linking a GPO to a site, domain, or OU, you control which users and computers within those containers receive the policy settings.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: A GPO cannot be linked directly to a user object.
claims.quote: You can't link a GPO directly to a user object.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: GPO processing proceeds in local, site, domain and OU order.
claims.quote:
1. The local GPO is applied.
2. GPOs linked to sites are applied.
3. GPOs linked to domains are applied.
4. GPOs linked to organizational units (OUs) are applied.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence
claims.claim: Settings from GPOs linked to Active Directory containers override local policy settings.
claims.quote: Policy settings from GPOs linked to AD containers override local policy settings.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence; Risks and limits: Precedence surprises
claims.claim: Within one container, the lowest GPO link order has precedence by default.
claims.quote: The GPO link with the lowest link order in the Group Policy Object Links list has precedence by default.

claims.where: What it is: Links and precedence; Governance controls: Enforced and Block Inheritance
claims.claim: Enforced is a GPO link property that takes precedence over Block Inheritance on a lower container.
claims.quote: Enforced is a link property and takes precedence over block policy inheritance, a container property.

claims.where: What it is: Security filtering; Why it matters
claims.claim: By default a linked GPO reaches user and computer objects in its container, with security filtering available to narrow the scope.
claims.quote: By default, a setting is applied to all user and computer objects within the container to which it's linked, but you can use security filtering to narrow the scope of the policy's application to a subset of users or computers.

claims.claim: Administrative Templates comprise .admx files and language-specific .adml files for registry-based policy settings.
claims.quote: Administrative Templates files are divided into .admx files and language-specific .adml files for use by Group Policy administrators.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes Windows Administrative Templates packages.
claims.quote: Administrative Templates (.admx) for Windows 11 2025 Update (25H2)

claims.claim: Microsoft Office has separate ADMX/L files for each release.
claims.quote: Microsoft Office has a separate set of ADMX/L files for each release.

claims.claim: Microsoft Edge has its own Administrative Templates.
claims.quote: There are two administrative templates for Microsoft Edge

claims.quote: you must create a Central Store in the sysvol folder on a Windows domain controller.

claims.claim: Central Store files replicate to all domain controllers in the domain.
claims.quote: The files that are in the Central Store are replicated to all domain controllers in the domain.

claims.quote: These policy settings are located at this registry path: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge.

claims.claim: Group Policy settings apply at computer startup and user sign-in.
claims.quote: Policy settings are applied at computer startup and user sign in.

claims.quote: Domain controllers check for computer policy changes every five minutes.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: GPO changes replicate within a site every 15 minutes.
claims.quote: Distributed File System Replication (DFSR) controls the replication of the SYSVOL folder. Within sites, replication occurs every 15 minutes.
claims.fix: Replace '(every 15 minutes within a site)' with '(the cited processing page says AD replication typically takes less than a minute within a site, while SYSVOL replication occurs every 15 minutes)'. This preserves the distinction explicitly documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-policy/group-policy-processing.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Narrowing security filtering
claims.claim: Removing Authenticated Users from Security Filtering removes both Read and Apply group policy permissions.
claims.quote: This action removes both the Read and the Apply group policy permissions from the group and all its members.

claims.claim: Group Policy is inherited and cumulative by default, reaching a container and its children.
claims.quote: By default, Group Policy is inherited and cumulative, and it affects all computers and users in an Active Directory (AD) container and its children.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Precedence surprises
claims.claim: A higher-precedence GPO can replace the same setting supplied by another GPO.
claims.quote: The sequence of GPO processing is crucial because each subsequent policy application can override settings applied by earlier policies.
